name: IST8310 3-axis magnetometer
description: iSentek three-axis AMR magnetometer measuring the magnetic field on X, Y and Z (±1600 µT on X/Y, ±2500 µT on Z, 3.3 LSB/µT, up to 200 Hz) over I2C, used as a drone/robot compass. Sold as: Rotorama RR-IST8310 V1.0 external compass module (4 pins in one row: SCL, SDA, GND, VIN), 4.5–5.5 V supply via its onboard 3.3 V regulator, 3.3 V I2C, address 0x0E (ADDRSEL pads select 0x0E or 0x0F).
eli5: A tiny compass chip: it feels the Earth's magnetic field in three directions so your board can work out which way is north.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 4.5–5.5 V (onboard regulator makes the 3.3 V the 3.6 V-max chip needs)

supplierQuery: Rotorama RR-IST8310 external compass IST8310 magnetometer module
buildNotes: Power VIN from 5 V (VBUS/VIN on the microcontroller board), not 3.3 V: the module is rated 4.5–5.5 V in. SDA/SCL are 3.3 V logic.
Address: ADDRSEL pads, left+centre bridged = 0x0E (14), centre+right = 0x0F (15). Never bridge all three. Run i2c.scan() to confirm.
Setup from the datasheet: soft reset (0x01 to 0x0B), check WHO_AM_I 0x00 = 0x10, write 0xC0 to 0x42 (pulse duration) and 0x24 to 0x41 (low-noise averaging).
Each reading: write 0x01 to 0x0A (single measurement), wait about 6 ms until bit 0 of 0x02 is set, read 6 bytes from 0x03: X, Y, Z, int16 LSB first. Field in µT = raw / 3.3.
Earth's field is about 25–65 µT. Keep the module away from motors, magnets, speakers and steel, and calibrate (min/max while rotating) before trusting a heading.

driver.code:
# IST8310 3-axis magnetometer (iSentek IST8310 datasheet v1.2 / v1.8), MicroPython driver.
# Power-on mode is stand-by. Datasheet 3.1.1: set PDCNTL (0x42) = 0xC0 and, for low noise,
# AVGCNTL (0x41) = 0x24. Each reading: write CNTL1 (0x0A) = 0x01 (single measurement), wait for
# DRDY (STAT1 0x02 bit 0), then read 0x03..0x08: X, Y, Z as 16-bit two's complement, LSB first.
# The chip returns to stand-by by itself. Sensitivity 3.3 LSB/uT (330 LSB/gauss).
import time

_REG_WAI = 0x00
_REG_STAT1 = 0x02
_REG_DATA_X_L = 0x03
_REG_STAT2 = 0x09
_REG_CNTL1 = 0x0A
_REG_CNTL2 = 0x0B
_REG_STR = 0x0C
_REG_AVGCNTL = 0x41
_REG_PDCNTL = 0x42

_DEVICE_ID = 0x10
_LSB_PER_UT = 3.3


def _s16(lo, hi):
    v = lo | (hi << 8)
    return v - 0x10000 if v & 0x8000 else v


class IST8310:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x0E, low_noise=True):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self._write(_REG_CNTL2, 0x01)  # SRST: run the power-on-reset routine
        time.sleep_ms(50)  # POR takes at most 50 ms
        wai = self._read(_REG_WAI, 1)[0]
        if wai != _DEVICE_ID:
            raise OSError('IST8310: WHO_AM_I is 0x%02X, expected 0x10 (check address)' % wai)
        self._write(_REG_PDCNTL, 0xC0)  # normal set/reset pulse duration (datasheet 3.1.1)
        if low_noise:
            self._write(_REG_AVGCNTL, 0x24)  # average 16x on X/Z and Y, >= 6 ms per sample

    def _write(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def _read(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def read_raw(self, timeout_ms=100):
        """Start one measurement, wait for DRDY, return raw (x, y, z) counts."""
        self._write(_REG_CNTL1, 0x01)  # single measurement mode
        time.sleep_ms(6)
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while not (self._read(_REG_STAT1, 1)[0] & 0x01):
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > timeout_ms:
                raise OSError('IST8310: no data ready')
            time.sleep_ms(1)
        d = self._read(_REG_DATA_X_L, 6)  # reading the data clears DRDY and DOR
        return _s16(d[0], d[1]), _s16(d[2], d[3]), _s16(d[4], d[5])

    def read(self):
        """Return the field (x, y, z) in microtesla."""
        x, y, z = self.read_raw()
        return x / _LSB_PER_UT, y / _LSB_PER_UT, z / _LSB_PER_UT

    def strong_field(self):
        """STAT2 INT bit: |X|+|Y|+|Z| exceeded 1600 uT."""
        return bool(self._read(_REG_STAT2, 1)[0] & 0x08)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ist8310 import IST8310

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
mag = IST8310(i2c)  # address 0x0E
while True:
    x, y, z = mag.read()
    print('X=%.1fuT Y=%.1fuT Z=%.1fuT' % (x, y, z))
    time.sleep(1)
